terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

sourceImage: attached-reference: single isometric view of a rounded two-storey courtyard medical clinic

referenceCamera.note: Isometric-like three-quarter view inferred from the visible front, left elevation, and roof. The supplied attachment is visible to agent vision but was not materialized as a local file, so camera values are an explicit visual estimate and must be overlay-refined if the source file is supplied.

objectClass.notes: Observable: a two-storey rounded rectangular building surrounds an open square courtyard. White fascia bands frame amber curtain walls; grass and pale paving form roof and ground ribbons.

reasoning: The identity depends on nested negative space: outer rounded footprint, roof promenade, and square courtyard opening.
Curtain-wall bays, mullions, parapet bands, grass borders, steps, furniture, and light fixtures are repeated systems.
Single-view rear geometry is inferred; visible front, left, roof, and courtyard relationships are high-confidence.

specDepthDecision.rationale: A shallow box cannot preserve the roof/courtyard negative space or repeated transparent façade system.

detailInventory.note: Manually authored from the visible attached reference after the crop scaffold was generated.

details.description: Repeated pendant bulb and stem cluster
Warm light line under entry steps

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

preSpecAssessment.sourceImage: attached-reference: single isometric view of a rounded two-storey courtyard medical clinic

definitionOfDone: At the reference isometric view, the model reads immediately as the same rounded two-storey medical clinic: square courtyard void, layered white fascia, green roof ribbons, warm modular glazing, front portal, two crosses, and landscaped stepped plinth.
At two orbit views, roof and courtyard remain genuinely volumetric and no façade collapses into a projection plane.
All named architectural assemblies remain independently clickable and separable by explode mode.

featureGroups.name: Courtyard and roof negative-space system
qualityCriteria: Square opening remains centered within the rounded roof ring and exposes the lawn below.
failureModes: courtyard is painted rather than open

featureGroups.name: Warm curtain-wall and mullion system
qualityCriteria: Front, left, upper, and courtyard glazing use repeated dark mullions and reveal warm interior depth.

featureGroups.name: Rounded white fascia and parapet system
qualityCriteria: All major floor and roof edges carry thick rounded white bands with legible bevel highlights.

featureGroups.name: Ground and roof grass ribbon system
qualityCriteria: Clipped green zones follow white curbs around roof, courtyard, front lawn, and right-side ribbon.
failureModes: grass becomes a full rectangular carpet
curbs do not follow grass silhouette

featureGroups.name: Medical identity and entry system
qualityCriteria: Roof and façade crosses are visible and the rounded glass entry portal aligns with stepped paving.
failureModes: entrance reads as an ordinary window bay

visualDeltaChecks: outer rounded-square silhouette and two-storey height ratio
courtyard aperture size and roof-ring thickness
front portal position relative to long glass façade
curtain-wall bay spacing and dark mullion value
green-to-white-to-grey material zoning on roof and plinth
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not fuse the roof slab, courtyard parapet, grass band, and walkway into one opaque mesh.
Do not represent the curtain-wall bay rhythm with a flat texture alone.
Do not omit the front and roof medical crosses.
Do not accept orbit views where the roof or walls collapse to planar cards.
mustNotDo: Do not fuse the roof slab, courtyard parapet, grass band, and walkway into one opaque mesh.
Do not represent the curtain-wall bay rhythm with a flat texture alone.
Do not omit the front and roof medical crosses.
Do not accept orbit views where the roof or walls collapse to planar cards.

mustMatch: two medical crosses and stepped entry

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

featureReviewTargets.name: Open courtyard and nested roof-ring system
Rounded white floor and parapet bands
Warm transparent façades and mullion rhythm
Ground and roof grass ribbons with white curbs
Stepped glass entry and medical crosses
Visible warm lobby furniture and pendant lighting

sculptPipeline.blockedReason: blockout requires a browser screenshot and self-correction review before structural-pass unlocks
nextRequiredEvidence: blockout browser render screenshot from your agent's browser/screenshot tool
AI vision score >= 0.7 with layer scores and mismatch critique
critical semantic feature scores from the same image pair meeting their individual thresholds
reviewHistory entry for blockout with action=continue

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: The chat attachment was available to agent vision but not as a local image path. Materials are procedural visual estimates, not recovered PBR.

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold
reference lighting copied without separating material readability

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: Rear and right elevations repeat the visible curtain-wall module language at lower confidence.
Wall thickness, structural grid, and interior floor plan are inferred for a stable real-time prop.
Grass is procedural texture plus sparse relief rather than millions of individual blades.
Glass transmission is tuned for interior readability, not physically exact optical simulation.

coordinateFrame.front: camera-facing side in the reference image
coordinateFrame.scaleReference: unit scale; adjust after first browser render

observations: Front and left elevations plus roof and courtyard are visible.
Outer white frame, amber glass, green ribbons, pale paving, and medical crosses are identity-defining.
Rear elevation, exact wall thickness, roof drainage, and interior plan are hidden and inferred.
